An open patch test with test material and breakdown products did not sustain dermal sensitization. Another subject had faint minimal erythema at 48-96h challenge. The study concluded dermal sensitization was not sustained.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1.625% AMP in body polish diluted to 1% in distilled water, 0.2 mL occlusive patch on interscapular region, 9 applications 3 times per week for 24 hours, 2-week rest, challenge on virgin site with 24-hour application, scoring at 24 and 72 hours
evidence.support_text: A repeated insult patch test in 105 subjects (initial 114) evaluated a body polish containing 1.625% AMP (diluted to 1%). The test material did not indicate potential for dermal irritation or allergic contact sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 110 subjects; occlusive patch on upper arm 3 days/week for 3 weeks; details not fully restated but assumed similar to previous RIPT (per 'methods described above').
evidence.support_text: An RIPT with 110 subjects tested a lipstick containing 18% Diisopropyl Dimer Dilinoleate. The lipstick formulation was not a sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 121 subjects (30 male, 91 female); 0.1 g/patch on upper arm under occlusive patch 3 days/week for 3 weeks; 12-20 day nontreatment period; challenge patches applied to original and previously untested sites; evaluation at 48, 72, or 96 h after challenge.
evidence.support_text: An RIPT with 121 subjects tested a lipstick containing 27% Diisopropyl Dimer Dilinoleate applied occlusively to the upper arm. During induction, two subjects had a response. The lipstick formulation was not a sensitizer upon challenge.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2.5% Sorbitan Isostearate, 201 subjects, occlusive patches of 0.2 g applied three times per week for 3 weeks to upper arm or back, 2-week nontreatment period, 72-hour challenge patch, reactions scored at 96 hours post application
evidence.support_text: Sorbitan Isostearate (2.5%) was tested in a RIPT using 201 subjects and did not induce a sensitization response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2.5% Sorbitan Isostearate; 201 human subjects; RIPT protocol
evidence.support_text: Sorbitan Isostearate at a concentration of 2.5% was negative in an RIPT using 201 subjects (CIR 1999).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20% in petrolatum, 55 participants
evidence.support_text: Decylene glycol (SymClariol) did not induce skin sensitization in an RIPT with 55 participants patch tested at a concentration of 20% in petrolatum.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 3.5% AMP in hair dye base diluted 50% in distilled water to 1.75%, 0.2 mL semiocclusive patch applied to infrascapular region, 9 applications over 3 weeks (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) with 24-hour removal, 10-14 day rest, challenge at virgin site with 24-hour application, scoring at 24 and 48 hours
evidence.support_text: A repeated insult patch test in 108 subjects evaluated a hair dye base containing 3.5% AMP (diluted to 1.75% in distilled water). No reactions were observed, and it was concluded the test material was a non-primary irritant and a non-primary sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 3.8% AMP in hairstyling gel, 0.02 mL in occlusive Finn Chamber patch applied to infrascapular region, 9 consecutive applications with 48-hour removal, 10-15 day rest, challenge at week 6 with scoring at 48 and 72 hours
evidence.support_text: A repeated insult patch test in 50 volunteer subjects using a hairstyling gel containing 3.8% AMP showed no evidence of sensitization. During induction, one subject had minimal/doubtful responses for patches 6-9 and another for patch 6. The challenge phase showed no sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 48 human subjects, ten induction patches and a single challenge patch with UV exposure
evidence.support_text: A repeat insult patch test (RIPT) with UV exposure was performed to evaluate phototoxicity of nail product containing 0.03% drometrizole in 48 human subjects. Ten induction patches and a single challenge patch with UV exposure were applied. In conclusion, the nail product containing 0.03% drometrizole was evaluated as nonirritating, nonsensitizing, and nonphotosensitizing.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 50% w/v in liquid paraffin, Finn chambers, 91 human subjects, induction and challenge phases
evidence.support_text: In a repeat insult patch test (RIPT) (Finn chambers) with 91 healthy human subjects, Glyceryl Linoleate (50% w/v in liquid paraffin) did not induce skin irritation or sensitization in the 74 subjects who completed the study.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 50% w/v in liquid paraffin, Finn chambers, 91 human subjects, induction and challenge phases
evidence.support_text: In the same RIPT, Glyceryl Laurate (50% w/v in liquid paraffin) induced mild, erythematous reactions during induction in most subjects and questionable reactions in seven subjects during the challenge phase, with reactions ranging from mild to moderate erythema (score=2).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 50:50 (w/w) mixture of 1,2-hexanediol and caprylyl glycol, effective concentration per ingredient = 10%, 56 participants
evidence.support_text: Skin sensitization was not observed in an RIPT with 56 participants tested with a 50:50 (w/w) mixture of 1,2-hexanediol and caprylyl glycol (Symdiol 68; effective concentration per ingredient = 10%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: human participants, RIPT, cyclomethicone (average n = 4) as test substance
evidence.support_text: In RIPTs, cyclomethicone (average n = 4) was neither an irritant nor a sensitizer in human participants.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: nine consecutive 24-h semiocclusive exposures (0.2 ml or 0.2 g); challenge after 10–14 days rest, single 24-h occlusive patch on naive site; scored 24 and 48 h post-application. Subjects: 104 completed (AMA Laboratories Inc. 1998a), 105 completed (AMA Laboratories Inc. 1998b). Product: SD Alcohol 40 (95%) at 47% in product (~44.7% SD Alcohol 40 in 1998a; ~44.6% in 1998b).
evidence.support_text: Two RIPT studies (AMA Laboratories Inc. 1998a, 1998b) tested a product containing SD Alcohol 40 (95%) at 47% (~44.7% and ~44.6% SD Alcohol 40, respectively) in 104 and 105 completing subjects. None of the subjects had any adverse reactions to the product; it was classified as a non-primary sensitizer to the skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: lipstick with 7.2%-9.4% Synthetic Beeswax; 896 human subjects; RIPT protocol
evidence.support_text: No irritation or sensitization was observed after a lipstick (7.2% to 9.4% Synthetic Beeswax) was tested in 896 subjects using an RIPT.

evidence.experimental_conditions: occlusive patches; eye defining pencil containing 1.68% Tristearin
evidence.support_text: An eye defining pencil containing 1.68% Tristearin was negative for allergic contact dermatitis in RIPT with occlusive patches. All subjects were contact lens wearers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: occlusive patches; eye enhancer cream containing 0.32% Tribehenin; 198 subjects
evidence.support_text: An eye enhancer cream containing 0.32% Tribehenin was negative for allergic contact dermatitis in RIPT with occlusive patches (198 subjects). All subjects were contact lens wearers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: occlusive patches; hand cream containing 0.38% Tribehenin; at least 200 subjects
evidence.support_text: A hand cream containing 0.38% Tribehenin was negative for allergic contact dermatitis in RIPT with occlusive patches (at least 200 subjects).

evidence.experimental_conditions: occlusive patches; lip cream containing 0.38% Tribehenin; at least 200 subjects
evidence.support_text: A lip cream containing 0.38% Tribehenin was negative for allergic contact dermatitis in RIPT with occlusive patches (at least 200 subjects).

evidence.experimental_conditions: product with 40% SD Alcohol 40 (95%); occlusive hypoallergenic patch; 0.2 ml or 0.2 g; nine consecutive 24-h periods; 10 to 14-day rest; challenge; 110 subjects (106 completed); ages 18-64
evidence.support_text: AMA Laboratories Inc. (1999a) performed an RIPT on SD Alcohol 40 (95%) in a product at concentration of 40% on 110 subjects (106 completed). None had adverse reactions, and it was classified as a nonprimary irritant and a nonprimary sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: product with 47% SD Alcohol 40 (95%) denatured with Brucine Sulfate; semiocclusive hypoallergenic patch; 0.2 ml or 0.2 g; nine consecutive 24-h exposures over 3 weeks; 10 to 14-day rest; challenge; 107 subjects (104 completed); 71 females, 36 males
evidence.support_text: AMA Laboratories Inc. (1999b) used an RIPT to evaluate a product containing 47% SD Alcohol 40 (95%) denatured with Brucine Sulfate on 107 subjects (104 completed). No adverse reactions noted, classified as non-primary irritant and non-primary sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: product with 72% SD Alcohol 40-2; occlusive hypoallergenic patch; 0.2 ml or 0.2 g; nine consecutive 24-h exposures; 10 to 14-day rest; challenge patch; 202 subjects
evidence.support_text: A second RIPT on 202 subjects with a product containing 72% SD Alcohol 40-2 found one panelist with a +1 reaction at 48-h reading of both challenge patches, but no reaction at 96-h; it was concluded that the product with 72% SD Alcohol 40-2 has a low potential for irritation and sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: product with 74% SD Alcohol 40-2; occlusive hypoallergenic patch; 0.2 ml or 0.2 g; nine consecutive 24-h exposures; 10 to 14-day rest; challenge patch; human subjects
evidence.support_text: Two subjects had reactions in the RIPT with a product containing 74% SD Alcohol 40-2, but it was concluded that the reactions were due to skin fatigue and not sensitization, and the sensitization potential of the product with 74% SD Alcohol 40-2 is very low if at all existent.

evidence.experimental_conditions: RIPT on 108 subjects (aged 19-65), product with 47% SD Alcohol 40 (95%), patches applied for 24 h every Monday, Wednesday, Friday for 3 consecutive weeks, challenge in week 6, reactions scored 24 and 48 h after removal.
evidence.support_text: AMA Laboratories Inc. (2001) tested SD Alcohol 40 (95%) present in a product at 47% in an RIPT. The tests originated with 110 subjects, but 108 subjects (aged 19 to 65) completed the patch tests. The testing laboratory used the exact same protocol as in the studies described above. No adverse reactions were observed, and the product with SD Alcohol 40 (95%) was classified as a non-primary irritant and a non-primary sensitizer to the skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: RIPT, 101 healthy participants (males and females), leg and foot gel containing 0.5% 1,2-hexanediol, semiocclusive patch on upper back, 24-hour wear, repeated applications.
evidence.support_text: A leg and foot gel containing 0.5% 1,2-hexanediol was applied to the upper back of each of 101 healthy participants (males and females) in an RIPT. Each site was covered with a semiocclusive patch that remained in place for 24 hours. The product did not induce skin irritation or sensitization in this study.

evidence.experimental_conditions: RIPT, 101 participants (males and females), foundation containing 0.112% pentylene glycol, 1x1 inch semiocclusive patch with 0.2 g product, repeated 24-hour applications on upper back.
evidence.support_text: A foundation containing 0.112% pentylene glycol was evaluated in an RIPT using 101 participants (males and females). A 1\" × 1\" semiocclusive patch containing 0.2 g of the product was applied repeatedly (24 hours of applications) to the upper back. It was concluded that the product did not have a potential for inducing skin irritation or allergic contact sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: RIPT, 56 participants, 20% test concentration in gel (effective concentration per ingredient 10%), semiocclusive patch, 24-hour wear, repeated applications.
evidence.support_text: A 50:50 (w/w) mixture of 1,2-hexanediol and caprylyl glycol (Symdiol 68) was evaluated in an RIPT involving 56 participants. At a test concentration of 20% in gel (effective concentration per ingredient = 10%), the mixture did not induce skin sensitization in any of the participants tested.

evidence.experimental_conditions: RIPT; 1.65% AMP in body polish; 0.2 mL of 1% dilution applied with semiocclusive patch to interscapular region; 24-hour exposure; 3 times per week for 9 induction applications; 2-week rest; challenge patch; human subjects (113 initial, 108 completed)
evidence.support_text: A RIPT was performed with a body polish (rinse-off) containing 1.65% AMP on 113 subjects (108 completed). The test material was prepared as a 1% dilution and applied with semiocclusive patch for 24 hours, 3 times per week for 9 induction applications. After a 2-week rest, a challenge patch was applied. No indication of dermal irritation or allergic contact sensitization was observed. The study concluded that the test material containing 1.65% AMP did not indicate a potential for dermal irritation or allergic contact sensitization.
